Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for acute central chest pressure starting a few hours prior while gardening, ongoing at time of call with dyspnea, diaphoresis, nausea, and left arm/shoulder radiation.
- High suspicion for acute coronary syndrome; ambulance activated, patient advised to keep door open and await EMS for ECG and hospital transfer as indicated. Noted aspirin allergy.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute chest pain concerning for ACS
  - Onset: A few hours prior to consult during light gardening.
  - Character: Central chest pressure “like someone sitting on my chest,” diffuse; radiates to left arm and shoulder.
  - Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath, sweating, nausea (no vomiting), feels heart beating faster currently (attributed to stress).
  - Currently ongoing at time of consult.
  - Risk factors: Smokes ~10 cigarettes/day for ~15 years; history of hypertension; overweight; sedentary lifestyle; family history—father died of MI around age ~60, mother with heart problems; hyperlipidemia status unknown (never checked).
  - Social/safety: Lives alone; door kept open for EMS access as advised.
  - Clinical impression: Suspected acute coronary syndrome (possible myocardial infarction). EMS activation arranged for urgent assessment (ECG and transport).

Issue 2:
- Hypertension (history reported)
  - Current antihypertensive medications: not documented.
  - Diabetes: denied.
  - Hyperlipidemia: never checked.

Issue 3:
- Aspirin allergy relevant to ACS management
  - Reaction: Swelling; described as mild, not life-threatening; patient has occasionally taken aspirin despite reaction.
  - Plan: Patient instructed to clearly communicate nature of aspirin allergy to EMS/hospital; clinician notes aspirin may still be considered despite allergy (to be decided by hospital team).

Medications:
- No current medications documented in this consult.

Allergies:
- Aspirin: swelling (mild), not life-threatening; patient reports occasional use despite reaction. No other drug allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Hypertension.
- Denies diabetes.
- No known hyperlipidemia testing to date.

Social History:
- Tobacco: ~10 cigarettes/day for ~15 years.
- Alcohol: ~7–8 pints of beer per week.
- Occupation: Restaurant owner (sushi shop).
- Activity: Generally low physical activity.
- Living situation: Lives alone.
- Weight: Patient reports being overweight.

Preventative History:
- Lipid screening: Never checked per patient.
- Other preventive care (cervical/prostate screening, fecal occult blood test, bone mineral density, mammogram, vaccinations, optometry, skin check): not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth visit; no vitals recorded.
- No physical examination findings documented.

Plan:
- EMS activated for urgent evaluation of suspected ACS; patient kept on the line until EMS arrival.
- Patient advised to keep front door open for EMS access.
- EMS to perform ECG and determine appropriate hospital destination and treatment.
- Patient to inform EMS/hospital of aspirin allergy and its characteristics.
- Handover to EMS planned upon arrival.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Comprehensive medication list and dosages; full past medical/surgical history; vitals and physical exam; lipid profile; detailed cardiovascular risk assessment; immunization and preventive screening history.
- Internal conflicts: Age unclear in dialogue; DOB provided as 1958-08-08 but ages stated inconsistently during conversation (conflict noted). Palpitations description somewhat ambiguous; patient reports heart “beating faster now” due to stress.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor conversational filler and brief inconsistencies.
